newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik aluminium plant eyes higher 1997 output.
newsitem.headline: Tajik aluminium plant eyes higher 1997 output.

text.p: Tajikistan's Tursunzade aluminium smelter hopes to raise output to 230,000 tonnes this year from 198,500 tonnes in 1996, a plant official said on Monday.

Chief engineer Lavrenty Gabrielyan said by telephone from Tursunzade that the smelter produced 90,000 tonnes of primary aluminium in the first half of this year compared to 100,000 tonnes in the same period last year.
But he was confident the plant -- located some 60 km west of the Tajik capital Dushanbe -- would meet its 1997 production target of 230,000 tonnes.
"We still have a lot of time until the end of this year, so we hope to reach the set target," he said.
But even if the smelter produced its planned 230,000 tonnes, this would be just half its record production of 460,000 tonnes in 1989.
Gabrielyan said the plant, commissioned in 1975, has never produced at its installed annual capacity of 500,000 tonnes.

The smelter -- the main source of revenue for the Central Asian state south of Russia which has been ravaged by four years of civil war -- has often been the focus of clashes among maverick bands vying for influence.

Last week mutinous Colonel Makhmud Khudoyberdyev, commander of the government's elite armoured brigade, defied official Dushanbe and declared he had assumed control over the area, including the smelter.
Gabrielyan said the recent events had not interrupted the plant's work, adding, "The work was never stopped and is going on despite the changing situation in our region."
